boundary_rationale: The row opens where the curse reverses generational direction: יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו (web:Ps.109.14 = oshb:Ps.109.14, “Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered”) turns from web:Ps.109.9-Ps.109.13’s forward-looking curses on his children and his posterity to the wicked man’s fathers and mother. A shared remembrance-root binds oshb:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.16: the verb opening יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו recurs as the noun זִכְרָֽם (web:Ps.109.15 = oshb:Ps.109.15, “their memory”) and again in the motive clause יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹ֥א זָכַר֮ (web:Ps.109.16 = oshb:Ps.109.16, “because he didn’t remember”). The curse then resumes as a clothing image: וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב קְ֭לָלָה (web:Ps.109.17 = oshb:Ps.109.17, “he loved cursing”) and וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ קְלָלָ֗ה (web:Ps.109.18 = oshb:Ps.109.18, “He clothed himself also with cursing”)—the cursing-noun shared by both verses is otherwise unattested in the book (sweep: 2 of 2 skeleton hits book-wide, both here). The unit closes on the verdict-label זֹ֤את פְּעֻלַּ֣ת שֹׂ֭טְנַי מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (web:Ps.109.20 = oshb:Ps.109.20, “This is the reward of my adversaries from Yahweh”), reverting to the plural “my adversaries” of web:Ps.109.1-Ps.109.5 before the direct petition opens at web:Ps.109.21.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off the motive clause and clothing image (web:Ps.109.16-Ps.109.20) as its own row was considered but rejected because the shared remembrance-root binds web:Ps.109.16 too tightly to web:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.15 to argue an independent seam.

device_notes: This seam is the psalm's most-debated internal division: the imprecatory register carried forward from web:Ps.109.6-Ps.109.13 runs on here under the same jussive grammar apart from the motive particle יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר at oshb:Ps.109.16 alone, whose clause runs through the wayyiqtols of oshb:Ps.109.17-18 (וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב, וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ) before the jussive resumes at oshb:Ps.109.19 (תְּהִי), the kinship reversal to אֲ֭בֹתָיו (oshb:Ps.109.14) marking the turn. The clothing-as-curse image (web:Ps.109.17-Ps.109.19) is this psalm's own device, not shared with the other five psalms of this span.
